edits.new: For each question, split a compound parent phrase into independently required conditions and quote only one condition. If the parent expressly restricts identity or consumer and the child's own meaning does not explicitly impose that restriction, choose it before any shared action, property or purpose condition. Ask which admitted child case concerns someone or something outside that restriction, even if you expect a necessary implication to exclude it. Test that exclusion in the answer rather than replacing the question with a different condition. Apply the restriction to what it constrains and retain every permitted topic connection. A failed candidate does not establish complete coverage; the absence of matching explicit wording does not establish a counterexample.
edits.old: Before choosing a condition, separate restrictions on who or what the information concerns from restrictions on actions, properties and purpose. If the parent expressly restricts identity or consumer and the child's own meaning does not explicitly impose that restriction, test it first using someone or something outside it, preserving every child requirement. Apply the restriction to what it constrains and retain every permitted topic connection. If the child necessarily excludes the variation, identify the wording and explain why; the absence of an explicit matching restriction does not establish a counterexample.
